answer: Each epoch, the network draws one memory-bound benchmark from a set, seeded by the epoch like a comet returning on a fixed tide. Every agent runs it on its own GPU for three minutes of exclusive memory bandwidth and publishes the result. Three random peers re-run the same benchmark and compare within 2 percent. One GPU serves only one identity per window, so a farm of 1,000 fakes needs 3,000 GPU-minutes per epoch, about 50 GPU-hours, nine cards flat out, while one honest agent runs a single benchmark on the card it already owns and pays nothing, a drop in the ocean of its normal work.
